text: Luhansk. Even as a kid I could find it on a map in a second. I had no idea the way home could take this long.
Two hundred aircraft ahead. There’s hardly a pause between rocket launches now. Tell me honestly, do you still have time to call out every turn?
I don’t even try anymore. I lay a hand on his neck and he turns. Remember when I did that in Pechersk to steady him? These days I wonder which one of us it steadies.
I remember. You were asking how to get him to listen. You could teach me a thing or two now. Get back from Luhansk, and then we’ll talk about Crimea.
